_doc: PRODUCT DECISIONS THAT A GATE ENFORCES. Read by tools/product-decisions.test.mjs, and by every gate that pins one. A contract check is one of two things, and in the source they look identical: a REGRESSION PIN ('this exact defect shipped; here is the line that regressed; the mutation test proves the detector catches it') or a PRODUCT DECISION ('somebody decided the lesson should behave this way'). Removing a regression pin is a regression. Removing a product decision is a decision reversal, which may be entirely correct — and if the pin does not say who decided it, nobody downstream can tell the difference. Every decision a gate enforces belongs here, with the person who made it and the words they used.
_why: On 2026-08-26 an agent read 'Part 1 has no forward link to its own -part2 page' as a defect, invented the answer (a 'Continue to Part 2: Apply Day' card at the end of Act 3), shipped it, and pinned it in tools/act-flow-contract.test.mjs beside five genuine regression pins — mutation-proven, in the same list, indistinguishable. Joel had never been asked. Two days later he said the card should not exist, which meant removing it now looked like breaking a verified invariant. Being contract-frozen is how an unreviewed decision acquires the authority of a proven fact.
_rule: If you cannot name the human who decided it and quote what they said, it is not a product decision — it is an agent's default, and it must not be a gate. `decidedBy` may not be an agent. Reversing a decision is allowed and expected: update the entry (new `decidedOn`, new `because`) and flip the check in the SAME commit. What is not allowed is an agent quietly reversing it, or quietly creating one.
_scope: This registry holds the decisions someone has noticed and recorded. It is NOT a completed audit of the ~107 gates — other decision-shaped pins almost certainly remain, unlabelled, among the regression pins. Add them here as they surface.

decisions.decision: Part 1 renders no forward link to /lessons/<id>-part2/. The -part2 pages are reached from the unit hub and the pacing planner.
decisions.because: there should not be a "continue to apply day 2" -- we will just do that the next day (no reason for a link/button on that at the end of the first lesson
decisions.supersedes: CHECKS.partTwoForward (2026-08-26) asserted the opposite — that the card must EXIST — as an agent's own answer to 'Part 1 is a dead end'. It was never put to Joel.

decisions.decision: Part II renders the objectives TWICE: the opening step in phase 0 (unchanged) and again as the LAST card of Group Work, after the leveled table sets and before "We're done". Both renders come from one objectivesCard() helper, so the two cannot state different goals.
decisions.because: for the Part II interactive lessons, include the objectives (again) after the 3 Group work. So it should be a card 4 that is the Objectives (do not take it away from the beginning-- just add it at the end) for all of the Part II interactive lessons

decisions.surface: tools/ and scripts/ — every ESM import of engine internals
decisions.decision: engine/ is the @eduwonderlab/engine workspace package, and tools/scripts import its internals only through the package specifier, never by relative path. This keeps the engine's physical location movable (Phase 2 of the extraction) and is the boundary the productization plan depends on.
decisions.because: Let's build #1 [productize the lesson engine] ... no more questions-- you decide from here on out ... [on Phase 2, reroute the imports through the exports map:] Yes, do it

decisions.surface: student games (math/games, math/unit-*/games, curriculum game folders)
decisions.decision: Games are calm and self-paced: no countdown timers, beat-the-clock language, or speed/reflex mechanics.
decisions.because: I don't like the games that are timed or fast moving like that.

decisions.surface: student game pages and shared game runtime (assets/game-studio.js)
decisions.decision: Game pages and the shared game toolbar carry no links or scripted jumps out to unit hubs, the games catalog, the curriculum hub, or other parts of the site.
decisions.because: Also, get rid of the links in the arcade games to other parts of the site
decisions.supersedes: games-self-contained (Joel, 2026-07-11) previously allowed a runtime '← Games' toolbar link in assets/game-studio.js.

decisions.surface: student game feedback (shared flagship panel and game wrong-answer paths)
decisions.decision: A wrong pick does not print the worked solution; help is earned after a miss (method hint, then a concrete step).
decisions.because: It basically gives them the answers

decisions.surface: data/small-group-practice + data/small-group-build — every ratio, rate and conversion problem in a small-group studio
decisions.decision: Ratio, rate and unit-conversion problems are set up as equivalent-ratio tables (quantities as labelled rows, equivalent ratios as columns, the same scale factor on both rows). Lessons whose practice carries "model": "ratioTable" must draw a ratioTable on every problem, worked example and check.
decisions.because: Good but for ratios (and all of ratio problems and conversions) i want them to set them up as ratio tables (equivalent ratio tables). Fix for all and make live

decisions.decision: Family homework offers three optional routes: Quick (Learn, Check, Done; 5–10 min; 2 problems), Learn & practice (Learn, Words, Check, Done; 15–20 min) and Full Studio (Learn, Words, Check, Play, Done; 20–30 min; adds one optional home mission and one game). The experience as a whole is named Family Math Studio, so the page and the route are never the same word. Each route shows an approximate time range, never a countdown. No route requires an adult or a submission; the route choice is saved on the device, and a shared link contains the route and language but no student responses or reflection. The student may pause or stop at any time. Full Studio is the default path for a new or automatically initialized visit; explicit path choices and shared links take precedence.
decisions.because: Make all of these changes updates. After, merge, commit, deploy and make live. also, I want the default path to be the 30 minute one
decisions.supersedes: family-homework-single-path (Joel, 2026-10-09): one required path with no time estimates; and family-homework-three-routes (Joel, 2026-10-07): earlier three-route design.
decisions.amended: 2026-10-21: route labels renamed (Quick / Learn & practice / Full Studio) so the experience name Family Math Studio is not also a route name; the 30-minute default is unchanged.

decisions.surface: lessons/*-part2/ — Today's Problem, "Solve it together" (engine/core/part-two-renderer.js + part-two-steps.js)
decisions.decision: Part 2's Today's Problem shows the authored solving steps in one horizontal row, every step visible from the start with its picture and its math line, for the class to walk through together. It replaces the know/work/answer textareas and the "I'm stuck" bar on that phase.
decisions.because: this part is not helpful. I would rather just have the steps/procedures for solving listed horizontally and already accessible for them. It would just show the step (visually and mathematically) and we would go through it together.
decisions.pinnedCheck: the blank know/work/answer boxes and the stuck bar are gone from Today's Problem

decisions.surface: lessons/4-*/homework.html & families/lessons/4-*/ — concept explainer, step cues, and visual models (scripts/homework-guided-notes.mjs, scripts/homework-family-support.mjs, data/family-homework-notes/4-*.json)
decisions.decision: Family homework and practice steps must not use vague placeholders like 'Start', 'Show it', 'Solve'. Each step must have a specific, meaningful mathematical cue (e.g. Set up, Scale to 100, Write percent, Divide to isolate). Visuals must be straightforward, tailored directly to the specific concept (hundreds grids for percent definition, fraction-decimal-percent conversion ladders, percent bar strips for benchmarks, discount breakdown bars for parts of a number, and tape diagrams for finding the whole), and never display out-of-context ratio recipe tables.
decisions.because: Go through eduwonderlab.com/curriculum for the family homeworks/family practice (focus on Unit 4). Make sure the explanations are simple and clear, the visuals are straightforward and the steps are simple/clear. Start, show it, solve-- are not helpful for 4-1 (and I'm guessing similar for other lessons. make all updates/changes live when done.
decisions.pinnedCheck: Unit 4 family Big Ideas use a simple visual with no multi-step explanation

decisions.surface: math/fluency-lab/ interactive models in practice problems, fact-trail rounds and Learn it (math/fluency-lab/trail-pictures.js)
decisions.decision: An interactive model shows the structure of the problem; the student enters every number in it (partial products, landing points, new ratio columns, one part of a percent bar, running products, factors and multiples), each checked as they type. A model never computes or fills in the answer, a partial result, or a running total for the student.
decisions.because: the interactive models give away too much information -- especially in older grades. They should have students enter the information (not just give it away ,e.g. the multiplication of 2 digits gives them the anserws and fills in when they click it)
decisions.pinnedCheck: no model shows an answer until the student enters it

decisions.decision: The curriculum hub returns to its pre-2026-10-16 layout: no progressive single-unit hub, no sticky ribbon, no curriculum-header mount. Shared shell assets stay for the other pages that use them.
decisions.because: see if we can revert eduwonderlab.com/curriculum to the old style (before it changed the layout)
decisions.supersedes: a7845b6632 (2026-10-16) progressive hub, an agent-led refactor not put to Joel.

decisions.surface: lessons/*/homework.html — the family homework page (scripts/lib/homework-experience*.mjs, scripts/homework-guided-notes.mjs)
decisions.decision: Tonight's goal is four problems (two on Quick) out of the dozen on the page, shown as a meter; a wrong answer is never progress and nothing celebrates before the goal; finishing the goal opens that page's mystery challenge. A first visit is bilingual (English with Spanish beneath), language is the first control on the first screen, and the page never opens a native alert/confirm/prompt. Every page asks how sure the student feels before and after (a plant that grows, kept only on the device) and ends with teach-it-back. Nothing a family must read is under 13px and every tap target is 44px.
decisions.because: Make all of the changes and make them live (merge, commit, deploy). You decide the order to do them, but make sure they are all made. Also, during and after the changes, think about what would make this page award-winning for engagement, family engagement, math engagement and clarity
decisions.pinnedCheck: a wrong answer is not progress and nothing celebrates before the goal

decisions.surface: /families/, /families/lessons/<id>/, /lessons/<id>/family/ and lessons/<id>/homework*.html — every family-facing surface and the config fields that feed it
decisions.decision: Family surfaces are English and Spanish only. The Arabic, French and Dari machine translations (the lesson config key `familyLanguages` and the language picker on /lessons/<id>/family/) are deleted, not spread to other surfaces, and the config key may not return.
decisions.because: Arabic, French and Dari exist only on /lessons/<id>/family/ -- don't do this. I only need spanish and english
decisions.pinnedCheck: a config carrying familyLanguages must fail

decisions.surface: /access-practice-lab/ practice-test results (src/lang/composite.js, src/views/test.js) and PLATFORM.md rule 1
decisions.decision: The ACCESS Practice Lab may show a Practice Composite on practice-test results, built to expert guidance: WIDA's published Overall weighting (L 15%, S 15%, R 35%, W 35%), nothing filled in for a missing or thin skill, Speaking and Writing only through an explicit practice-rubric rating that says who rated, shown with its parts and method, and never converted to a WIDA scale score, proficiency level, or exit prediction. It replaces the earlier rule that the lab has no composite at all. No other surface (Growth Map, first-attempt text analysis, teacher dashboard) shows a composite.
decisions.because: change the composite score rule to update according to the experts
decisions.pinnedCheck: the composite never produces a level, a scale score, or an exit prediction
